chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Hashimi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, who said: My brother Ja'far ibn Isa narrated to me, saying:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the fasting of the day of Ashura and what people say about it, so he said: 'Regarding the fasting of Ibn Marjanah (may Allah curse him), you ask me about that. It is a day that only the pretenders from the family of Ziyad, due to the killing of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), fasted. It is a day that the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) considered ill-omened, and the people of Islam considered ill-omened. The day that Islam and its people considered ill-omened is not fasted, nor is blessing sought from it. And Monday is a day of ill-omen; Allah took His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) on it. And the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) were afflicted only on Monday, so we considered it ill-omened, and our enemies considered it blessed. And on the day of Ashura, Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed, and Ibn Marjanah considered it blessed, and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) considered it ill-omened. So whoever fasts them and considers them blessed, he will meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with a wiped (blessed) heart, and his gathering place will be with those who established the fasting of them and considered them blessed.'

key_terms.ابْنُ مَرْجَانَةَ: Ibn Marjanah, a specific historical figure associated with the Umayyads, used here as a symbol of the 'pretenders'
key_terms.تَشَاءَمَ: To consider ill-omened / to regard as unlucky
key_terms.صَوْمُ عَاشُورَاءَ: Fasting on the day of Ashura

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and significance of fasting on the day of Ashura according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the Umayyad governor Ibn Marjanah fasted on Ashura to claim legitimacy, whereas the Ahl al-Bayt viewed it as an ill-omened day of martyrdom. This distinction highlights the theological concept of *Tashayyum* (taking as an ill-omen) versus *Tabarruk* (seeking blessing), where fasting on Ashura signifies alignment with the enemies of the Prophet's family. Consequently, those who fasted on this day with the Umayyads will meet Allah with a 'wiped heart,' indicating a loss of spiritual vitality.
